text:
The main issue here is that the 'high end cpus' you guys use for benchmarks don't account for the real world at all. Steam hardware survey says 3060 is the card most people have. That's a real world representation. The 3060 is what any card you talk about, needs to be compared to. It doesn't help a population of 3060 owners to know the B580 out performs a 4060 8gb card (when the 3060 12gb out performs that at higher settings/resolutions) or a B580, when the 3060 is still being sold new, is cheaper than a B580/4060, AND doesn't suffer from the same hardware design flaws Nvidia continues to pursue. 

It's not a matter of 'bottlenecks' and 'low end CPUs aren't going to benefit as much' because the world doesn't limit their play to the few games you benched. In fact, there is a pretty large library of games people play, many of them old. There are also games where the engine is hard capped to a frame rate (60fps) with any CPU that isn't dead being able to play it at that frame rate. Pair B570 with that random CPU, that game runs at 60, regardless of Cyberpunk running at something way lower. 

Nobody is going to be playing cyberpunk on a GPU they have to budget for, because that's not a good experience. A lot of these games you bench aren't going to be the games people buy a 570 to play, unfortunately. If by some chance I'm trying to play Cyberpunk or something similar on a potato PC, I'm accepting whatever frames I get, and probably buying a b570 to get more frames over waht ever I get with an iGPU or some GT430 or 710 or whatever the new basement budget king GPU is. 

Real world is: I want to game, I have a PC, let's adapt and get whatever enjoyment I can from it, even if it's not the big boy high fps OLED experience. Intel might be doing the better job of reaching a real world audience to give them options, rather than forcing them to continue to buy 12gb 3060s to avoid the pitfalls of being stuck with a 4060 or unable to find a b580. This video is only really helpful to the people willing to stomach a 4060's performance issues at medium settings, decide if a B580 is a better option than the B570, considering their CPU. If I am trying to step up from a 3060, trying to get more performance or better visuals, better features, or access to DLSS 4? 

I have to step it up to a 4070 Super at starting double the price. GPU Makers have really made the decision as simple as: does it have more than 8gb vram? If yes, it's probably better than whatever you have. Meanwhile, Nvidia is gonna try and sell you another generation of 8gb video cards. 

There are no good options, only whatever side-grade at a higher price we are willing to accept.
